label: TP
reason: Both alerts (java/xss, java/tainted-format-string) correctly identify user input flowing to the response writer. The sink is response.getWriter().printf(bar, obj) where bar originates from request.getParameter. Although the code replaces the last character of bar with 'Z', the preceding characters remain unsanitized user input, allowing XSS payloads (e.g., '<script>') to be rendered. Thus, both alerts are True Positives.

evidence.note: User input acquired via getParameter assigned to param, then passed to doSomething.
doSomething assigns param to bar and replaces only the last character with Z, leaving prefix unsanitized.
Sink: bar is used as format string in printf, exposing unsanitized user input to response.
